title.narrative: World Health Organization Core Voluntary Contributions 2022-2027

description.narrative: This investment will enable the provision of voluntary core contributions to the World Health Organization (WHO) between 2022-2027. The investment will support WHO to deliver on its overarching mandate, approach, goals and objectives as outlined its Constitution and General Programme of Work. In addition, this investment will enable Australia to advance the efficient and effective operations of WHO in the Western Pacific Region.

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

description.narrative: Australia is currently the fourth highest contributor of core voluntary contributions to the World Health Organization (AUD32 million for the 2022-23 biennium, or six per cent of total global CVC funding of USD326.2 million). While Australia’s CVC funding is flexible, enabling WHO to direct funding to activities under its General Programme of Work, agreed priorities under the DFAT-WHO Strategic Partnership Framework include improving health outcomes and health security in the Indo-Pacific. In 2022-23, WHO programs provided targeted support to small island developing states in our region, with a focus on quality essential health services, delivered irrespective of gender, age or disability, in Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands; and healthy environments that promote health and sustainable societies in Fiji.

The World Health Organization (WHO) is a key development partner for Australia in the Indo-Pacific and globally, driving action on critical health challenges in partnership with the multilateral system. In the 2024-25 biennium, Australia is the fifth highest contributor of core voluntary contributions (CVC), delivered flexibly, enabling WHO to direct funding under its General Programme of Work. This includes improving health outcomes and health security in the Indo-Pacific and advancing pandemic prevention preparedness and response. In 2024, WHO mobilised public health specialists to respond to disease outbreaks in our region, including leading the Pacific Joint Incident Management Team’s response to outbreaks of pertussis and mpox, delivering rubella vaccination in Solomon Islands, and preparing for a tuberculosis vaccine trial in Indonesia. In May 2024, the World Health Assembly adopted amendments to the International Health Regulations supporting collective action on infectious disease threats and clarifying WHO's role in public health emergencies. WHO demonstrates a strong commitment to incorporating considerations of gender, age, and disability throughout its policies and programs.
